source_fields.unit_cost: Each complete response $(g_j(x))_{j=1}^{k}$ costs one call. Its first two components can simulate one full stochastic gradient–Hessian response or one HVP. Internal computation is free. When the source algorithm has random cost, the fixed-cap implementation retains its budget truncation and joint-event success constants.
free_operations: Global solution of known models, exact real arithmetic, and linear algebra are free. Information about the unknown external function is available only through the stated oracle.

view_override_policy.limitations: Mechanical merge does not certify consistency or mathematical identity. Narrative qualifications and source conditions remain authoritative.

source_fields.uniformity: One algorithm must work for all admissible instances and oracle laws; an average guarantee over a hard distribution alone is insufficient.

description_paragraphs: The base error is
$$\mathcal{E}(\widehat{x})=\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2.$$
The criterion uses the gradient norm itself. Squared norms, expectations, and probability guarantees are recorded separately and are not substituted automatically.
Return $\widehat{x}\in \mathbb{R}^d$.
The objective $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ is bounded below.
The objective has a finite infimum, and the public initial point $x_0$ satisfies $f(x_0)-\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)\le\Delta$.
Fix $k\ge3$ and $f\in C^k$. For every $1\le j\le k$, $D^jf$ is $M_j$-Lipschitz, with $M_1=\beta$.
The derivative estimates need not arise from one scalar sample loss. Conditional moments and independence are specified by the oracle.

description_paragraphs: Each complete stochastic response specified under ORACLE costs one unit; each fresh-sample response within a batch is charged separately.
The resource budget is a fixed worst-case cap on every execution path. Initialization, stopping checks, and all actual responses in a batch are included.
Arithmetic, linear algebra, tensor operations, storage, and global solution of known models are free. Bit complexity, communication, and wall-clock time are not counted.

Random sample identities and internal data are hidden. Reuse through opaque handles is governed strictly by the coupling field.

description_paragraphs: At any $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$, draw a fresh sample and return the complete $(g_j(x))_{j=1}^{k}$. Conditional on the history and query, every derivative estimate is unbiased and satisfies
$$\mathbb{E}[g_j(x)\mid\mathcal{H}]=D^jf(x),\qquad\mathbb{E}[\|g_j(x)-D^jf(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\mid\mathcal{H}]\le\sigma_j^2.$$

Each call uses a sample independent of the previous history. Sample identities are hidden and cannot be reused, and no function value is returned. Estimates of different derivative orders need not arise from the same scalar sample loss.

The public inputs are $x_0$, the target accuracy, and $d$, $k$, $\Delta$, $\beta$, $M_2$, $(M_j)_{j=1}^k$, $(\sigma_j)_{j=1}^k$, $\varepsilon_g$, $\sigma_1$, $\sigma_2$. Numerical constants are admissible bounds and need not equal the sharp constants of the instance. The objective, unqueried derivatives, minimizer and minimum value are hidden.

Find an approximate first-order stationary point of the full objective, namely $\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2\le\varepsilon_g$. The interaction interface and admissible outputs are specified under ORACLE and OUTPUT, respectively.

internal_computation_restrictions: Zero-respecting: nonzero coordinates of queries and outputs must have been activated by earlier replies; the definition is that of ACDFSS20, Appendix H.1.
